primary_claim: A 3-layer, 4-head transformer trained from scratch on the Mess3 hidden-Markov process learns to linearly encode the process's fractal belief-state geometry in its final-layer residual-stream activations, replicating and walking through the mechanism behind Shai et al.'s belief-state-geometry result.

effect.value: transformer loss roughly matches the ideal belief-state model's loss (~0.83 average per-token loss over 10000 prompts), lying approximately on the y=x line across 1000 prompts

contradicts_or_qualifies: notes that unlike Mess3, in processes like RRXOR similar next-token predictions do not imply proximity in belief space, so belief-state geometry is not fully captured in final-layer activations alone (per Shai et al. Sections 3.2-3.3, arXiv:2405.15943)
stated_future_work: explore how transformers represent processes with distinct belief states that have similar next-token predictions, in upcoming blogposts
gain a more precise understanding of how stacked attention blocks and layers communicate and coordinate to implement belief-state updates
limitations_stated: the residual stream projection is not as sharp as expected, though it may sharpen with more training time
the arguments relating final-layer activations, softmax invertibility, and belief geometry are described as handwavy with room to be made more formal
the clean linear correspondence between belief states and final-layer activations breaks down for processes like RRXOR where the mapping matrix S is not invertible
quote: we have seen that transformers are capable of internalizing complex, structured belief states by reflecting their fractal geometry within the residual stream
